description: Nowind geometry: every length derives from one input, --F, after Affine UI. At the root --F is the fluid body size (--text-base, 14px at a 360px viewport to 18px at 1240px), so controls, radii, icons and shadows grow with the type. A .scope sets --F to its own font size (1em), so a part of the page can be pinned or resized.

scopes.rule: --F is declared twice: :root { --F: var(--text-base) } follows the fluid type scale; .scope { --F: 1em } follows the scope's font-size. Everything derived is declared on :root and on every .scope, so it recomputes in both. --F is registered with @property as a <length>, so it resolves to px.

inputs.use: The base size. At the root it follows --text-base, so geometry grows with the viewport; in a .scope it is that scope's font size.
slot = slope × F + offset.

See --radius-slope. Raised from Affine's -6px so the nested step (control − margin) is 5px at 16, not 3px, which read as sharp on keycaps and nested items; every step gains 2px and nesting stays exact.

See --q-slope.

Massimo's length unit; every shadow layer is a multiple of it, so shadows scale with the scope's font size.

control.formula: slot − F − 1, at least the border

control.use: Height of a button or input.
Outer edge to text where no icon sits.
Height of a small control and of a control nested in another.
Inline padding of a control on a side with text; class px-control.
Inline padding on a side that holds an icon, so the icon's box sits one margin from the outer edge.

Inline padding of a small control on an icon side.

notes: The fluid --space-* scale lives in theme.space.css (generated by scripts/utopia.mjs).

--truncate-bleed (0.3em): the block padding, with the same negative margin, that a truncate label in a control takes, so its overflow clip reaches below the baseline and keeps descenders after the cap-height trim.

radius.use: A card, popover, toast; class rounded-md.
A part inside a control or an item inside a popup; class rounded-xs.
A card, popover or toast; class rounded-md.
A sheet or hero panel; class rounded-xl.

breakpoints.rule: Tailwind v4 names and values. CSS can't read a custom property inside @media, so scripts/utilities.mjs reads these values when it writes the sm: … 2xl: variants.

icons.rule: After Affine UI's <ui-icon>: an S-square box with the glyph centred. Phosphor's weights follow the size: ph-bold at sm, ph (regular) at md, ph-light at lg.

tokens.use: Small glyph, the small text step (0.875 × F, as text-sm), so it matches text-sm labels in chips, badges and toolbars; class icon-sm. Carets use it.

tiers.rule: After Affine's space tiers. .tier-product (1×, the default), .tier-content (font +2px, spacing 1.5×) and .tier-brand (font +4px, spacing 2×) are scopes: --F and everything derived from it recompute inside them. --tier multiplies --page-margin and --section-gap; --tier-inner (half strength, at least 1) multiplies --surface-padding and --dialog-padding.
tiers.selectors: .scope, .tier-product, .tier-content, .tier-brand share the scope declarations in theme.geometry.css, theme.space.css and theme.shadows.css.

tokens.use: A placed element pads itself by this, so two neighbours make one gutter; class p-grid-inset.
Page edge padding where there is room; class px-grid. No tier multiplies it.
Page edge padding on narrow screens; class px-grid-compact.
The collapsed sidebar rail; class w-rail.
A column of text; class max-w-measure.
The page width at which the sidebar docks beside the content.

marks.rule: A mark (checkbox, radio, switch, slider) is an icon's drawing size: sm F, md between F and the slot (the default), lg the slot. The reset draws native inputs with these; classes mark-sm and mark-lg pick another size.

nesting: After Affine UI, one unit runs the whole scale: each radius step is one margin (M) from the next (xs = control − M, sm = control, md = control + M, lg = control + 2M, xl = control + 3M), and the padding between levels is the inset (I = M − border). So a bordered container padded p-inset holds items one radius step down, concentrically: (r + M) − (M − B) − B = r. Pairs: rounded-md p-inset holds rounded-sm; rounded-lg p-inset holds rounded-md; rounded-sm p-inset holds rounded-xs. Any other padding uses rounded-inner (the parent's radius minus its padding and border).

containers.use: @sm: to @2xl: apply a layout class when the nearest @container is at least that wide, so a component adapts to the slot it sits in rather than the window. In px like the breakpoints, because a query can't read a custom property; scripts/utilities.mjs reads these values.

chrome.use: A fixed size for a site's own settings and tool panels, which must not follow the root size or the tier. Put text-chrome with scope on the panel: --F becomes 14px there, so its controls, gaps and radii are fixed too (a 30px control).

glyphs.source: Phosphor Icons (MIT), caret-down-bold and check-bold, inlined as SVG data URIs so Nowind loads nothing extra
glyphs.use: Masks for the drawn indicators: the caret class, the select's picker icon and the selected option's checkmark. Each is painted in currentColor at --icon-sm.

geometryContract.description: Which height, padding, gap and corner each kind of part in an example takes, so every part of one kind is built the same way. The rows read the Affine geometry above: control height 4n − 26, margin M, inset M − border, radii one M apart. A lint and a rendered pass (?audit=geometry) will check the examples against it. Every row is written in regular (primitive) classes, the ones examples use: control lengths, space steps, radius steps and rounded-inner.

kinds.identify: button, select, field box, tab, menu item, option
kinds.padding: px-control (steps in at an icon edge)
kinds.current: 135 parts; all on h-control px-control gap-gutter

kinds.identify: a button or link inside a toolbar, field, toast or alert
kinds.corner: rounded-inner at a surface's padding; rounded-xs one inset inside a control

kinds.gap: none: items touch; a divider between groups
kinds.corner: rounded-sm; items h-full rounded-inner (icon items aspect-square)
kinds.current: 9 boxes, 27 items, all on the contract

kinds.height: h-nested, or no fixed height when it holds a remove button

kinds.identify: count, avatar, step number, timeline icon
a selectable card: a label wrapping a radio or checkbox

kinds.padding: one line: py-xs ps-xs pe-sm; titled: p-xs
kinds.gap: gap-gutter between icon and text (as toasts and controls); titled: gap-3xs between lines
kinds.current: 4 one-line at gap-xs, 4 titled at gap-3xs

rules: Nesting: an element at a container's padding takes rounded-inner, the container's radius less that padding and border; rounded-xs is the radius one inset inside a control.
Even insets: a part at a container's end sits the same distance from every edge it faces.

No text closer than the container's padding to its edge; label text sits in a span so px-control and px-nested can find the icon edges. The rendered check takes the padding of the text's nearest padded box: at tiny sizes (a 12px root on a phone, about 1.5px) the geometry's own padding is accepted; a painted box with no padding still needs 2px.
Side by side, controls share a height; a box holding controls is a control tall.
Markers with aspect-square, size-* and rounded-full render as true squares and circles.
A clipping box (overflow-hidden) never hides its content at any width.

layoutContract.description: How parts sit on the page at every width and root size. ?audit=layout measures each rule on the rendered page; node scripts/review.mjs form runs it over every page at 375, 768 and 1280px and 12, 16 and 18px roots.

rules.rule: Nothing scrolls the page sideways at any width.
Text stays inside its box: long words and URLs wrap, or the box scrolls (overflow-x-auto) or truncates (truncate).
A painted box pads its start and end alike, unless an icon, a nested control or a badge sits at the shorter edge.
Text stacked in one column shares a start edge; an indent comes from a marker, icon, avatar or control at the start, not from stray padding.
A border never lies on the same edge of a bordered container: a table's last row draws no rule inside a framed table, a card's footer draws no line on the card's own border.
A child of a flex or grid container with a gap carries no margin in that direction: the gap is the spacing, and a margin on top of it doubles up.
